$comment: Declarative benchmark cases for eval/benchmark_runner.py.
Every `ground_truth` block below is copied verbatim from an existing golden
set under eval/golden/, and each block names its source in `golden_source`.
tests/test_scenarios.py re-checks that correspondence, so a scenario cannot
drift away from the golden set it claims to come from. Ground truth that is
invented rather than copied would make every accuracy number meaningless.
`repo` selects the corpus. Flow scenarios use tests/fixtures/callflow because
that is the corpus eval/golden/flow.jsonl was built against; everything else
uses the repository root.
Scoring axes, all deterministic and requiring no LLM:
recall        - every listed filepath appears in the output
symbol_recall - every listed symbol appears in the output
order         - the listed symbols appear in that relative order (flow only;
a call path out of order is a wrong answer, not a short one)
unresolved    - citations in the output that name a file or symbol which
does not exist, counted as fabrications
One entry in eval/golden/ai_db.jsonl targets ai_db/server/http_server.py,
which was deleted when the HTTP transport was removed. It can never be
recalled, so recall@10 over that golden set is capped at 0.975. It is left
in place because editing the golden set changes what the CI gate measures,
but every recall figure should be read against that ceiling.

$comment: Matrix 2. analyze formats and pack formats are DIFFERENT sets and the runner
asserts it: `outline` and `prose` are valid for analyze and must be REJECTED
for a pack. `analyze --format json` is the only format that emits
meta.tokens_out_formatted, and the runner checks the emitted value equals the
token count of the bytes actually received.
pack_queries: how is the config file validated

$comment: Matrix 4. `summary` and `structure` are documented as byte-identical; the
runner checks that instead of trusting the doc, and reports a finding if
they ever diverge. `expand --depth` cannot be benchmarked as a subprocess
-- ref handles are process-scoped -- so it is recorded as not-measurable
rather than faked.
Matrix 3. Conditions are generated by eval/matrix_configs.py into a scratch
dir and each is synced before querying, so latency reflects a built index.
A condition listed in `cuda_conditions` is SKIPPED with an explicit note
when no GPU is present -- reported as skipped, never as a zero.
`sync_root` bounds the corpus, and it is the SAME for every condition,
which is what makes the comparison valid: a config comparison needs one
corpus held constant, not a large one. `ai_db/` is the library source; it
excludes tests/ and eval/, which the retrieval benchmark showed to be the
largest confound in the index. The runner records the file and chunk count
per condition so a reader can verify the corpora really do match.
Bounding this matters: a full-repository hybrid_cuda sync took ~30 min for
2,023 chunks (~890 ms/chunk), against ~73 ms/chunk measured on a 12-file
corpus, so a full sweep of 7 conditions did not fit in any reasonable
timeout. That superlinearity is unexplained and worth its own investigation.
Measured on this host (RTX 3070 Laptop), same model and device, 189 chunks:
bfloat16  26.6s   7.1 chunks/s
float16   29.2s   6.5 chunks/s
float32  594.8s   0.3 chunks/s   <- 22x slower than bfloat16
A full float32 index over sync_root is therefore ~50 minutes against ~2
for bfloat16, so the dtype sweep is opt-in rather than in the default run.
Note `embedding.dtype: auto` resolves to None on an accelerator, meaning
'load whatever the model ships in' -- bfloat16 for Qwen3-Embedding -- so
the default already takes the fast path and the gate is not choosing
badly. Only an explicit float32 pays the 22x.

$comment: Matrix 5. Agent-realistic: config x transport, scored on a held-out half.
Transport dominates configuration. Measured on this repo, same index:
CLI subprocess, lexical   ~240 ms per call, every call
CLI subprocess, hybrid   ~10.5 s per call, every call (model reload)
persistent MCP           8-286 ms first call, then 0.2-1.4 ms
So a CLI-only harness does not add noise to the hybrid comparison, it
inverts it: the highest-recall config looks like the slowest by three
orders of magnitude, purely because of how the process is launched.
Config selection reads the `tune` half of the golden set and reporting
reads `holdout`, because choosing a config to maximise recall@10 on the
same 40 queries that gate CI would manufacture the number being reported.
The split is deterministic and stratified by module; see eval/heldout.py.
`doc_weight` is swept on hybrid only. A lexical config has no fusion
weight, so sweeping it there would report a no-op as if it were a
datapoint. `conditions` defaults to lexical + hybrid so the run needs at
most one CUDA index build; add the vec0 and dtype variants to sweep them.
Raw-context baselines, both reported. `files` reads the top N matching files
whole, which is what an agent does with `cat`. `windows` reads matching lines
plus context, the strongest thing an agent can do with a shell. Quoting only
the first would flatter ai-db. The limits are set generously on purpose.
The LLM arm is OPTIONAL and defaults to off. With no API key the runner sets
llm.measured = false and every LLM metric to null. It does not invent TTFT,
generation time or a hallucination rate.
Quality metrics (recall, symbol recall, order, unresolved citations) are
deterministic functions of the output text and need no LLM, so they are
always reported. The `unresolved` count is the structural stand-in for
fabrication: a pack that cites a symbol or file that does not exist has
invented it, and that is checkable without a model.
`answer_tokens` is the assumed reply length used by the cost projection. It
is a declared assumption, labelled as such, not a measurement.
